Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CellSystemCond.text: This is a mathematical proposition about shared functions, matrices and analytic witnesses. No Accept function or byte decoder is defined here, so the displayed checker-to-condition arrow remains an external soundness obligation.

Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CertificateCla.text: The decimal restrictions are the digest’s algebraic deductions from the paper’s chosen constants. This declaration supplies generic premises and does not prove that one numerical data set meets them.

Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.isExtendedCert.text: This constructor first replaces the decay bound by a sufficiently large constant and takes the named analytic bridge results as arguments. The closed cell-system corollaries supply those bridge results.

Breakdown.Cert.HH.text: The formal forcing space is represented on the unit time circle using solenoidal Fourier data. It is connected to physical space-time fields by projection and reading theorems.

Breakdown.Cert.Internal.AtProfile.coerci.text: Lean implements absorption by replacing the model with the approximate profile and dividing the coercive coefficients and row weights by the appropriate transfer factor. This prepares the normalized certificate used in the solver.

Breakdown.Cert.Internal.ExtendedBordered.text: The formal proof adds and subtracts the identity on the finite multiplier block inside a finite-rank perturbation. Thus compactness applies to the full bordered operator, including the pins.

Breakdown.Cert.Internal.FreeEnergyLocal..text: The exported FreeEnergyLocalHolds statement retains only a continuous scalar enstrophy function. This internal theorem retains the continuous Fourier-gradient curve itself.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedAdjointEnclosureH.text: This proof assumes the normalised certificate with multiplier weight one. The general positive multiplier weight is transported by extendedUnitWeightHolds before the normalised construction.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedAdjointPairingHol.text: The proof tests the adjoint-defect condition with zero perturbation and the non-solenoidal part of the adjoint. That forces the adjoint to equal its solenoidal projection in the relevant L2 space.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedDataContinuityHol.text: The theorem proves continuity of the pin target gap and of the projected defect paired with each compact solenoidal test. It does not require strong continuity of the chosen residual representative in the forcing norm.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedExistsZeroHeldHol.text: This theorem takes IsNormalExtendedCertificate: multiplier weight one, model equal to profile, zero gap and zero form shift. The general construction first applies profile absorption and multiplier-weight normalisation.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedHeldExistsUniqueH.text: The uniqueness conclusion concerns the normalized certificate's held class at a fixed parameter. It is not a uniqueness theorem for all periodic similarity profiles or for the selected parameter.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedHeldLimitHolds_of.text: Lean passes to limits of solutions of the nonlinear held equation. The paper paragraph instead passes to limits of linear solves indexed by an independent quadratic-force variable.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedHeldMapsToHolds_o.text: The formal theorem preserves the same radius and supremum budgets for a nonlinear map at a fixed parameter. The paper's simultaneous map on parameters and independent nonlinear forcing is a different construction.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedHeldNonzeroHolds_.text: The formal conclusion rules out vanishing almost everywhere in time and space. Later smoothness turns this into pointwise nontriviality.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedSigmaProfileOfHel.text: The construction chooses the certificate period at the selected parameter and adds its correction to the approximate field. Its theorem type returns only an existential weak profile, so it hides the parameter, pinning identities and quantitative bounds.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedStiffEnclosureHol.text: The proof uses the normalised multiplier weight. Its stiff coordinates are the complement of adjointSet, matching the weighted-ball part of the parameter domain.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedSupBoundHolds_of.text: The formal bound uses the actual certificate period divided by its selected twist. It bounds the essential supremum of the gradient and does not assume pointwise-in-time bounds on the forcing.

Breakdown.Cert.freeEnergyLocalHolds_of.text: Lean states an integrated identity for a continuous periodic representative of the squared gradient norm. The displayed derivative identity is its differential form wherever that scalar derivative exists.

Breakdown.Cert.heldDist.text: This distance is used on the class satisfying the two held bounds. Completeness and lower semicontinuity are established separately before the contraction argument.

Breakdown.Cert.productBoundHolds_of.text: The formal theorem bounds both the physical nonlinear field and its projected Hilbert-space representative. The time supremum is initially essential, and the weighted energy is identified with physical derivatives by a reading theorem.

Breakdown.Cert.sizeZ.text: The formal sizeZ has unit multiplier weight. The reduction to that normalization rescales the forcing fields and multipliers; weightedEnergy retains the physical spatial weight.

Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.pivotCoun.text: This theorem gives positivity of the root form. The total leaf form is positive on the same subspace only after composing it with signedTreeLowerBound.

Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.signedTre.text: The tree theorem compares the total leaf form with a root form that still includes the root front. Nonnegative root front, positive pivot coverage and a column-count bound enter only in the positivity step.

Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.stateTerm.text: Lean permits the auxiliary subspace to be a graph (L u, u) and allows a finite set of physical coordinates on which the form is independent. It performs the dimension argument after restricting away those coordinates.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.ShapeParam.text: The formal symmetry order is a variable positive natural number. The reported value 19 and half-period twist 2 are facts about the intended numerical instance, not values selected by this declaration.

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.angularModeB.text: The statement gives almost-everywhere bounds for Fourier components of weak fields and includes an additional curl-gradient inequality. The displayed formula presents the two bounds needed for the velocity and gradient.

Breakdown.CertCell.exteriorConditionSoun.text: The formal statement separately handles ray exteriors and a square exterior. The latter requires zero azimuthal frequency and a reflection condition, so the scalar inequality is only one part of the exterior premise.

Breakdown.CertCell.labelPhase.text: The Lean time variable is the digest’s theta; its azimuthal angle is the digest’s varphi. The spatial height ratio uses coordinate 2 because Lean indexes the three coordinates from zero.

Breakdown.CoerciveWeak.RowMultiplierIneq.text: The formal inequality is generic in the coercivity and pin weights. The displayed values 3/50 and 1000 specialise that algebra to the paper’s chosen constants.

Breakdown.DiscreteDichotomyInternal.rec_.text: This is a general forward recurrence identity. Applying it to the stable projection preserves the homogeneous term coming from the chosen initial correction.

Breakdown.DiscreteDichotomyInternal.tail.text: The series carries powers of Θ because its forcing is normalised to a bounded sequence. Its inverse operator already projects onto the exceptional range.

Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData.defect.text: The extended input uses a separately supplied weak Hessian and an orthogonal pressure-gradient representative. It does not require a globally classical second derivative or a chosen scalar pressure at this stage.

Breakdown.FarField.farFieldDecay_holds.text: The formal decay proof uses an integral equation, weighted kernel estimates and derivative bootstraps. It does not invoke Chae–Wolf as an external premise and also proves pressure-gradient decay.

Breakdown.FarField.periodicLerayProfileE.text: The statement returns only existence of a smooth profile. SmoothFieldOfOrbit retains the velocity identity for a chosen mild orbit, while further transport is needed to recover the original correction with its norms and pins.

Breakdown.FarField.smoothFieldOfOrbit_ho.text: The L6 to L12 to L∞ estimates in this section describe the paper. This formal theorem obtains a smooth representative through Fourier symbols, local Picard smoothing and overlapping time windows.

Breakdown.Freq.X.text: X is a closed subspace of Fourier L2 in the Lean. The velocity map and embedding theorems connect it to the physical homogeneous space.

Breakdown.Freq.bilinCompact.text: The linked proof uses total boundedness of frequency-truncated images and a controlled high-frequency tail. The preceding Rellich proof is the paper’s physical-space explanation.

Breakdown.Freq.bilinCompact_holds.text: This export states compactness for coefficients in the dense test space. The paper extends to arbitrary coefficients by the bilinear bound; the formal transfer argument instead uses dense-coefficient compactness as its input.

Breakdown.Freq.bilinX.text: The kernel is defined through its symmetric trilinear pairing. The test-field formula identifies the heat and divergence-free projection represented by the displayed operator.

Breakdown.Freq.testDense_holds.text: The whole-space formal transfer can choose compact solenoidal data from a dense subspace. It does not require the particular vector-potential cutoff used in this paragraph.

Breakdown.Freq.trilinear_holds.text: The formal proof bounds the trilinear pairing against test vectors, then uses the L2 and L6 heat bounds. It does not directly state the displayed L3/2-to-homogeneous-H1 mapping estimate.

Breakdown.Held.testSetZero_of.text: The raw update is defined inside this proof. A nearest-point retraction appears in the separate compact-convex theorem to extend its domain to a box; it does not replace the enclosure proof for this parameter update.

Breakdown.IsPerturbation.text: The formal domain records the velocity, weak gradient, weak Hessian and combined similarity transport as separate fields. It requires square integrability of the transport field and the Laplacian trace, without separate global bounds on time differentiation and spatial drift.

Breakdown.MonodromyStatement.text: One period is split into k short intervals so that each linear step is invertible by a norm bound. The monodromy is the rotated product of these step maps.

Breakdown.Periodic.ApproxSizes.Internal..text: This estimate is stated for a similarity-profile slice. The physical-time estimate in the digest also uses the similarity change of variables.

Breakdown.Periodic.R3Factor.text: The formal factorization applies to a compact test-field coefficient and a restriction operator. Approximation of the orbit by such coefficients is a separate input to the assembled transfer.

Breakdown.Periodic.ShellData.text: Lean stores restricted gradient columns in three L2 spaces and the restricted velocity in L6, using their product norm. This is an equivalent local control to the sum of norms displayed here, rather than a literal definition of that sum.

Breakdown.Periodic.approxFieldProperties.text: The linked theorem uses a fixed cutoff on the unit torus before periodization. The displayed whole-space radius is obtained by rescaling that construction; it is not the theorem's literal parameter.

Breakdown.Periodic.approxPeriodic.text: Lean periodizes by a wrap map on the unit cube and introduces a small blow-up time. The digest first uses a large physical torus and then rescales it.

Breakdown.Periodic.approxResidualSmall.text: Lean bounds a sequence of rescaled time-piece residuals by a geometric factor times a quarter power of the initial time scale. The digest uses a continuous weighted-time norm and a large torus period.

Breakdown.Periodic.breakdownOnTorus_of_p.text: The exported endpoint excludes a global smooth periodic-velocity solution with arbitrary smooth pressure. Moving-frame reduction connects this endpoint to the periodic-pressure class used by the mild construction.

Breakdown.Periodic.comparisonSmall.text: The formal comparison provides any prescribed tolerance after shrinking the blow-up time. The explicit large-period decay rates in the digest belong to the paper's comparison proof.

Breakdown.Periodic.cutoffField.text: Lean writes the cutoff as the cutoff times the field plus the cross product of its gradient with the potential. This is the product-rule expansion of the displayed curl.

Breakdown.Periodic.cutoffGradientClose.text: The formal gradient conclusion is an arbitrary-tolerance limit as the similarity scale tends to zero. It does not export the displayed radius power as a named bound.

Breakdown.Periodic.fieldSpace.text: The formal ambient space includes the zero Fourier mode. The paper's mean-zero homogeneous presentation is therefore not the literal definition of this space.

Breakdown.Periodic.freeHeatComparison.text: The formal result makes the restricted free-heat discrepancy smaller than any chosen tolerance at sufficiently small scale. It does not export the displayed power of the large torus period.

Breakdown.Periodic.heatDivFreeComparison.text: The formal comparison is an arbitrary-tolerance limit on restricted projected heat flows as the scale tends to zero. Its proof uses Fourier integrals and lattice sums, while the digest here presents the paper's explicit Oseen estimate.

Breakdown.Periodic.rightInversePerturb.text: The formal inverse perturbation lemma uses a defect at most one half and returns an inverse with norm at most twice the original bound. Its proof invokes the geometric-series inverse.

Breakdown.Periodic.shellInverseTransfer.text: The theorem transfers an inverse for an abstract equation built from restriction, local interaction and time-piece evolution operators. The displayed continuous-time construction explains the corresponding paper argument; its symbols are not the theorem's arguments.

Breakdown.PeriodicSimilarityProfileExist.text: This formal premise also requires uniform second spatial derivative and pressure-gradient decay. The pressure bridge described below is an analytic argument, not a proved conversion from the printed hypotheses in this source.

Breakdown.TransferHolds.text: This abstract conclusion chooses initial data in any dense submodule and retains a rescaled error bound with some positive exponent. It does not by itself state the full smooth physical Theorem 1.1 bundle.

Breakdown.WeakProfile.weakOrbitOfParts_h.text: This interface takes the named analytic bridge propositions as arguments and returns an existential mild orbit. TopStatements supplies those bridges; the interface does not export the selected correction or its pins.

Breakdown.breakdown_on_space.text: The endpoint excludes a global smooth solution with a uniform energy bound. It does not package the displayed blow-up rate or the error estimate on one constructed solution.

Breakdown.breakdown_on_torus.text: The endpoint excludes a global smooth solution whose velocity is periodic. It does not state the local H1 comparison with the profile.

Breakdown.compactPiece_of.text: The simple coefficient paths are dense, and the compact operators are closed in operator norm. This supplies the general time-dependent coefficient step.

Breakdown.compactSimple_of.text: The proof cuts off the last epsilon of the integral and bounds that tail by a quarter-power estimate. A compact convex hull handles the remaining integral.

Breakdown.contraction.text: The Lean uses a bounded sequence of normalised interval pieces, with a factor θⁿ on the quadratic term. The displayed continuous weighted convolution is the paper’s route to the corresponding nonlinear bound.

Breakdown.dichotomyHolds.text: The conclusion records two separated radii, geometric power bounds and surjectivity on the finite exceptional range. The displayed sums are consequences after choosing an intermediate decay rate.
